name: Acral Self-Healing Collodion Baby

criteria.description: Presence of a tight, shiny collodion membrane localized to acral areas at birth
Spontaneous shedding and resolution of the collodion membrane within the first few weeks of life without intervention
No evidence of systemic or generalized ichthyosis or other skin disorders on follow-up

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: acral collodion membrane at birth, spontaneous resolution within weeks, and absence of systemic skin disease.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and based on characteristic presentation and natural history.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Edema of the dorsum of hands
Edema of the dorsum of feet

other: Histopathology if performed shows compact orthokeratosis without epidermal abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Generalized collodion membrane covering entire body
Persistent scaling and hyperkeratosis after birth
Genetic mutations in TGM1 or related genes

redFlags: Failure of collodion membrane to resolve within 3-4 weeks
Development of systemic symptoms such as fever or growth delay
Signs of secondary skin infection or sepsis
references: Orphanet: Acral Self-Healing Collodion Baby - ORPHA:281127
Rajpopat S, Moss C, Mellerio J, et al. The collodion baby: a review of 50 cases. Arch Dermatol. 2011;147(6):681-686.

Oji V, Tadini G, Akiyama M, et al. Revised nomenclature and classification of inherited ichthyoses: Results of the First Ichthyosis Consensus Conference in Sorèze 2009. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2010;63(4):607-641.
